title: Optimal Consumption and Investment with Energy-Efficiency Adoption
summary: This arXiv paper (econ.GN) presents a theoretical model integrating consumption, investment, and energy-efficiency adoption under uncertainty. The authors develop new definitions of rebound and backfire effects, formalize welfare implications for optimal subsidy design, and model technology diffusion across heterogeneous agents. A German single-family home case study illustrates the results.
key_points: Authors: Anthony Britto, Carlos Oliveira, Max Kleinebrahm
Proposes unified framework for consumption, investment, and energy-efficiency adoption under uncertainty
Develops new definitions of rebound and backfire effects integrated into subsidy design model
Adoption threshold and post-adoption strategies depend on agent wealth, introducing financial conditions as a channel for technology adoption
Energy-efficiency adoption shown to be welfare improving in the main
German single-family home case study demonstrates subsidy policy can steer aggregate energy consumption
